rot.pawnChain.ideia.francesa.e1: Attack: let us think from Black's side. A pawn chain is a line of pawns of the same colour, linked on the diagonal: each one defends the one in front. The rear one is the base; the front one, the head.
rot.pawnChain.ideia.francesa.e2: This is the French Defence, Advance Variation. The white chain runs from d4 to e5. The e5 pawn is a wedge: an advanced, supported pawn that blocks the e6 pawn and takes the f6 square away from the black knight.
rot.pawnChain.ideia.francesa.l1: The c7 pawn advances to c5 and attacks the d4 pawn, the base. A pawn move that attacks the chain to open it is called a pawn break.
rot.pawnChain.ideia.francesa.l2: The c2 pawn goes to c3 and defends the base.
rot.pawnChain.ideia.francesa.l3: The knight goes to c6 and also attacks the d4 pawn.
rot.pawnChain.ideia.francesa.l4: The g1 knight goes to f3 and defends the d4 pawn once more.
rot.pawnChain.ideia.francesa.l5: The queen goes to b6 and backs up the attack on the base, behind the c5 pawn. Now Black prepares the capture on d4.
rot.pawnChain.ideia.francesa.l6: In positions like this, the chain is usually attacked at the base: no pawn defends it, and if it falls, the head is left without support. The other break is the f7 pawn going to f6, against the wedge. The position decides which one works.
rot.pawnChain.ideia.contra.e1: Attack: again with Black, in a game played on Lichess. The white chain runs from e4 to d5: the e4 pawn is the base.
rot.pawnChain.ideia.contra.e2: The f5 pawn touches the base on e4. Note the g5 bishop as well: the e7 bishop attacks it, and only the f3 knight defends it.
rot.pawnChain.ideia.contra.p: Find the break that captures the base of the white chain.
rot.pawnChain.ideia.contra.certo: The pawn captures the base on e4 and attacks the f3 knight, which defends the g5 bishop.
rot.pawnChain.ideia.contra.revela: The f5 pawn captures the base on e4 and attacks the f3 knight. If the knight moves away, the g5 bishop is left undefended.
rot.pawnChain.ideia.contra.err.e7g5.1: The bishop captures the g5 bishop, but it only trades pieces, without touching the chain.
rot.pawnChain.ideia.contra.err.e7g5.2: The knight recaptures on g5, and the position is equal.
rot.pawnChain.ideia.contra.err.e7g5.3: Back to the position: attack the base before trading the bishops.
rot.pawnChain.ideia.contra.err.c7d8.1: The queen goes to d8 and joins the e7 bishop against the g5 bishop, but from behind it.
rot.pawnChain.ideia.contra.err.c7d8.2: The bishop captures the h6 knight before being captured, and White is slightly better.
rot.pawnChain.ideia.contra.err.c7d8.3: Back to the position: use a pawn against the white chain.
rot.pawnChain.ideia.contra.fora: That move does not attack the chain. Use the f5 pawn.
rot.pawnChain.ideia.contra.volta: Try again: capture the base of the chain.
rot.pawnChain.ideia.contra.l0: On e4, the pawn attacks the f3 knight. If the knight moves away, the e7 bishop captures the g5 bishop.
rot.pawnChain.ideia.contra.l1: The g5 bishop captures the e7 bishop before losing its defender.
rot.pawnChain.ideia.contra.l2: The pawn captures the f3 knight. Now the e7 bishop is attacked by the king, and the f3 pawn attacks the e2 knight and the g2 pawn: White cannot save everything, and Black has a decisive advantage.
rot.pawnChain.ideia.contra.l3: In positions like this, the break that captures the base leaves the head without support and opens lines for the pieces. Here it worked because the pawn also attacked the knight that defended the bishop.
rot.pawnChain.ideia.proprio.e1: Attack: now with White, in a game played on Lichess. The white chain runs from d4 to e5, and the e5 pawn is a wedge: advanced and supported by the d4 pawn.
rot.pawnChain.ideia.proprio.e2: The wedge controls the f6 square, near the black king. No black pawn can contest it: there is no black pawn on e7 or g7.
rot.pawnChain.ideia.proprio.p: Find the move that uses the square the wedge controls.
rot.pawnChain.ideia.proprio.certo: The queen goes to f6 with check, defended by the e5 pawn and the d7 knight.
rot.pawnChain.ideia.proprio.revela: The queen goes to f6 with check, on the wedge's square, and attacks the d8 rook. No black piece can capture it, and the e5 pawn and the d7 knight defend it.
rot.pawnChain.ideia.proprio.err.f3f7.1: The queen captures the f7 pawn, but away from the wedge's square it neither gives check nor attacks the rook.
rot.pawnChain.ideia.proprio.err.f3f7.2: The black queen goes to g7 and offers the trade: without queens, Black has rook against knight.
rot.pawnChain.ideia.proprio.err.f3f7.3: Back to the position: look for the square the e5 pawn controls.
rot.pawnChain.ideia.proprio.err.d7f6.1: The knight occupies f6, but leaves d7 without giving check.
rot.pawnChain.ideia.proprio.err.d7f6.2: The rook captures the d4 pawn, the base of the chain: the wedge loses its support, and Black has a decisive advantage.
rot.pawnChain.ideia.proprio.err.d7f6.3: Back to the position: occupy f6 with the piece that gives check.
rot.pawnChain.ideia.proprio.fora: That move does not use the f6 square. Play with the queen or the knight.
rot.pawnChain.ideia.proprio.volta: Try again: occupy the square the wedge controls.
rot.pawnChain.ideia.proprio.l0: On f6, the queen gives check and attacks the d8 rook.
rot.pawnChain.ideia.proprio.l1: The black queen goes to g7 and blocks the check.
rot.pawnChain.ideia.proprio.l2: The queen captures the d8 rook with check, and White wins material.
rot.pawnChain.ideia.proprio.l3: In positions like this, the wedge gives the pieces a square in the opponent's camp that no pawn can contest. The position decides whether that square leads to the king or is just a good outpost.
rot.pawnChain.demos.regra.1: Attack demonstration: again with White. The black chain has its head on c4, supported by the b5 and d5 pawns.
rot.pawnChain.demos.regra.2: Note the a4 pawn, next to the b5 base, and the black pieces behind it.
rot.pawnChain.demos.regra.l.3: The pawn captures the b5 pawn and attacks the a6 bishop and the c6 rook at the same time.
rot.pawnChain.demos.regra.l.4: The bishop recaptures on b5 and removes the pawn that attacked both pieces.
rot.pawnChain.demos.regra.l.5: The rook captures the bishop: White wins a piece, and the c4 pawn has lost one of its supports.
rot.pawnChain.demos.regra.l.6: Without the b5 base, the c4 head has only one support left, and the b-file opens for the rooks. Here the break won material; in other positions, it only weakens the chain.
rot.pawnChain.demos.regra2.1: Attack demonstration: the white chain runs from f4 to e5, and the e5 pawn is a wedge.
rot.pawnChain.demos.regra2.2: The wedge controls the f6 square, near the black king.
rot.pawnChain.demos.regra2.l.3: The knight goes to f6 with check, supported by the wedge.
rot.pawnChain.demos.regra2.l.4: The black queen captures the knight: if the king went to h8, the white queen would mate on g8.
rot.pawnChain.demos.regra2.l.5: The e5 pawn recaptures on f6. Now the queen threatens mate on g7, defended by the f6 pawn.
rot.pawnChain.demos.regra2.l.6: In positions like this, the wedge's square is a door to the enemy king: when it leads to mate, it is worth more than any pawn plan.
rot.pawnChain.demos.excecao.1: Attack demonstration: Black has just played the f7 pawn to f6, a break against the e5 wedge.
rot.pawnChain.demos.excecao.2: Behind the wedge, the g5 queen is on the same rank as the black queen on d5.
rot.pawnChain.demos.excecao.l.3: The e5 pawn captures the f6 pawn with check and leaves the rank.
rot.pawnChain.demos.excecao.l.4: The bishop captures the pawn that gave check.
rot.pawnChain.demos.excecao.l.5: The queen captures the d5 queen, which was left exposed.
rot.pawnChain.demos.excecao.l.6: The break opened the rank for the white queen. In positions like this, breaking before the pieces are ready opens lines for the opponent: the position decides the moment.
rot.pawnChain.pratica.quebra.enunciado: The black chain runs from b5 to c4. Play White and find the best move.
rot.pawnChain.pratica.quebra.fim: The pawn captured the base on b5. After the a6 pawn recaptures, the king goes to b4 and captures the b5 pawn; without it, the c4 pawn has no support and falls too.
rot.pawnChain.pratica.quebra.err.c3b4: 29.Kb4? attacks the b5 pawn, but after 29...bxa4 30.Kxc4 the position is equal.
rot.pawnChain.pratica.cunha.enunciado: The black d4 pawn is a wedge, supported by the c5 and e5 pawns. Play Black and find the best move.
rot.pawnChain.pratica.cunha.fim: The queen went to e3 with check, on the square the wedge controls, and mated on f2, defended by the g3 bishop.
rot.pawnChain.pratica.cunha.err.g3f4: 25...Bf4+? moves the bishop off g3, and after 26.Qg2 White defends the king and has a decisive advantage.
rot.pawnChain.pratica.cunha.err.g3h4: 25...Bh4+? moves the bishop off g3, and after 26.Qg2 White defends the king and has a decisive advantage.
rot.pawnChain.pratica.valeAqui.enunciado: Both chains are locked on the queenside. Play Black and find the best move.
rot.pawnChain.pratica.valeAqui.fim: The knight gave check on f6, and the rook mated on g6. Here the chain did not matter: in positions like this, a mate comes before any pawn plan.
rot.pawnChain.pratica.valeAqui.err.d5f4: 41...Nf4+? gives check, but after 42.Kh6 the king attacks the g7 rook, and the position is equal.
rot.pawnChain.ideia.contra.err.h6f7.1: The knight goes to f7 and also attacks the g5 bishop, but the e4 base is still standing.
rot.pawnChain.ideia.contra.err.h6f7.2: The bishop captures the e7 bishop. After the recapture, the e4 pawn can capture the f5 pawn, and White is better.
rot.pawnChain.ideia.contra.err.h6f7.3: Back to the position: use the f5 pawn against the base of the chain.
rot.pawnChain.pratica.quebra.err.c3d4: 29.Kd4? heads for the centre, but after 29...Kb7 30.Kc5 c3 31.bxc3 bxa4 the black a4 pawn runs to promote, and Black has a decisive advantage.
rot.pawnChain.pratica.valeAqui.err.g7g4: 41...Rxg4? captures a defended pawn: after 42.Kxg4, Black is lost. Look for checks first.
rot.pawnChain.pratica.cunha.err.g3e1: 25...Be1+? moves the bishop off g3, and after 26.Qg2 White defends the king and has a decisive advantage.
42...Rxg4? captures the pawn, but 43.Rd6+ and 44.Rxf6 capture the knight, and Black is lost. Look for the check that mates.
